title: אזור פצאל (Fasael area, enclosure north of Nahal Fasael)
author: (staff officer for archaeology team, with Y. Porath)
location_note: North of the Nahal Fasael stream bed; map reference printed '1914/1623' (E/N order as printed; 32.05 N 35.44 E).
notes: Large enclosure: square courtyard about 120 m a side and a walled built area 111 x 40 m with a central building; one occupation layer; 1st-century BCE pottery and a coin of Jannaeus. The excavators suggest a Hasmonean farm abandoned after a short time, replaced by Herod's Phasaelis to the south. No aqueduct seen between the Fasael springs and the enclosure.

features.period: farm built in the Hasmonean period (1st-century BCE pottery, coin of Jannaeus)
features.quote: בעת הסקר נחשפה בריכה קטנה

features.period: not dated in this report

title: יריחו: תולול אבו אל-עלייק (Jericho, Tulul Abu el-Alayiq)
author: E. Netzer (with A. Lass)
screen_note: Built-site excavation at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).
location_note: Both banks of Wadi Qelt at its outlet: north wing opposite the sunken garden and the south tell (Kelso and Baramki's tell 1), the north tell (tell 2); a round tower about 1 km west of the north tell at the ascent of Tariq el-Hindi; no map reference.
notes: North wing of Herod's winter palace: reception hall 29 x 19 m, two courts, bathhouse with round frigidarium, opus reticulatum and quadratum; parts still in use at the end of the Second Temple period; a 2nd-century CE building burnt; last occupation end of the Byzantine period. North tell: late Hasmonean palace (central building about 65 x 50 m) with the plastered surrounds of the large swimming pool (HA47-018), which the excavator links with Josephus' account of the drowning of Aristobulus III; the surrounds went out of use when the Herodian artificial mound and garden covered them. Round tower 10.8 m in diameter probably of the end of the Second Temple period. The coin hoard is probably the one reported in HA 47 (same count and ruler).

features.subtype: previously unknown pool about 90 x 45 m
features.period: belongs to the Herodian palace in one of its phases
features.quote: נראה שבריכה זו שייכת לארמון ההרודיאני

features.period: Hasmonean palace, end of the Hasmonean period, still standing in Herod's first years

features.period: coins of Mattathias Antigonus (Hasmonean)

features.site: about 1 km west of the north tell

features.period: not dated

features.subtype: branching tunnel system hundreds of metres long (2-3 m high), partly timber-supported in the artificial fill; rock-cut steps into the upper cistern
features.period: probably the Bar Kokhba fighters (2nd-century CE lamps)
features.quote: קשורה כנראה בפעילות אנשי בר כוכבא

features.subtype: large miqveh with a stepped immersion pool and an adjoining water store linked by a pipe (the second miqveh found on the mountain)
features.period: First Revolt
features.quote: מכיל בריכת טבילה מדורגת וסמוך לו אוצר מים

title: רוג'ם אבו מוח'ייר (Rujm Abu Muhayir)
author: Z. Yeivin (with I. el-Fani and D. Bakar)
screen_note: Not in the gazetteer; the text places it on the road leading west from Fasael (gazetteer name) at the pass between the Jordan Valley and the hills. INFERENCE: at about the western edge of the Z2 box.
location_note: On the road west from Fasael, at the pass between the Jordan Valley and the hills; no map reference.
notes: Round building of three concentric rings, 19.40 m across, with radial rooms; large pithos sherds probably of the end of the Iron Age. No feature of the eligible classes.

title: ירושלים: הגבעה הצרפתית (Jerusalem, French Hill, three burial caves)
author: A. Kloner and R. Sivan
location_note: East slope of French Hill, edge of the WIZO day-care plot (near HA51-025); no map reference.
notes: Third cave: crosses incised on the wall and on lamps; Christian burials, perhaps of the Byzantine farm or a nearby monastery.

features.subtype: square chambers with central pit, benches and three kokhim in each of three walls; rolling stones in place; three plain ossuaries in one; a trough grave under a second burial in the other
features.period: Second Temple period; Herodian pottery of the 1st century CE
features.quote: שתיים מהמערות הן מימי בית שני ומערה שלישית זמנה בתקופה הביזאנטית

features.subtype: chamber with arcosolia on three walls, two burial places each; two burial phases
features.period: Byzantine (pottery and many lamps)
features.quote: שתיים מהמערות הן מימי בית שני ומערה שלישית זמנה בתקופה הביזאנטית

title: ירושלים: מנחת (Jerusalem, Manahat, rock-cut tomb with a lead coffin)
author: Y. Gat
location_note: Manahat, shelter foundations; no map reference.
notes: Decorated lead coffin with cupids; two men; gold earrings, gold and glass beads, gold ring with an engraved shrimp, gold threads.

features.subtype: rock-cut tomb with a decorated lead coffin
features.period: end of the 2nd or beginning of the 3rd century CE (coffin)
features.quote: יש להניח שזמנו של הארון מסוף המאה הבי

title: חדשות בקצרה: דיר אל-חטב (brief news: Deir el-Hatab near Shechem, rock-cut caves)
author: I. el-Fani (staff officer for archaeology team)
screen_note: Sub-item of the brief news; the text places Deir el-Hatab near Shechem (gazetteer name).
location_note: Hill south-east of the village of Deir el-Hatab near Shechem; no map reference.
notes: Three rock-cut caves exposed after robbing.

features.subtype: cave with niches cut in its walls like the known columbaria
features.period: not dated
features.quote: חצובות גומחות בדומה לגומחות הקולומבריה

features.subtype: two caves with eight kokhim and a central pit (1 x 1 m); one robbed
features.period: coins and lamps of the 1st-2nd centuries CE in one (the printed order is 2nd-1st)
features.quote: נמצאו מטבעות ונרות מן-המאות הבי-האי

title: חדשות בקצרה: רוג'ייב (brief news: Rujeib south-east of Shechem, burial cave)
author: I. el-Fani
screen_note: Sub-item of the brief news; the text places Rujeib south-east of Shechem (gazetteer name).
location_note: Rujeib, south-east of Shechem; no map reference.

features.subtype: burial cave 3.5 x 3.5 m with four large kokhim; four intact glass vessels and lamps
features.period: 1st-2nd centuries CE (the printed order is 2nd-1st)
features.quote: במערה ארבעה כוכים גדולים

title: חדשות בקצרה: עין סמיה (brief news: Ein Samiya, salvage excavation by a new road)
author: W. Zeidan (Ramallah district inspector)
screen_note: Sub-item of the brief news. The text layer reads 'עין ממיה'; read as Ein Samiya (INFERENCE: the ס/מ confusion is systematic in this text layer; Ramallah district, by the ancient cemetery).
location_note: By the ancient cemetery of Ein Samiya, on both sides of the wadi; no map reference.

features.subtype: rock-cut winepress paved with white mosaic
features.period: probably Byzantine
features.quote: נחשפה גת חצובה בסלע מרוצפת אבני פסיפס

features.subtype: 13 burial caves, mostly robbed; bronze weapons and pottery in three
features.period: Middle Bronze Age II B
features.quote: נחפרו 13 מערות קבורה

title: ח' מרג'מה (עין סמיה) (Kh. Marjama, Ein Samiya)
author: A. Mazar (with A. Barhum and S. Yankelevitch)
location_note: Hill at the end of a long spur above Ein Samiya; settlement of about 40 dunams; no map reference.
notes: Iron Age II fortified town (tower on a podium, wall 4 m wide plus retaining walls), houses with 9th-8th century BCE pottery; bronze bowl. Earlier suggestion of a cult place on the cupmarked rock surface (not tested by the report). Identification proposals: Ephraim (Albright), Baal-shalishah (Kallai).

features.subtype: rock surface with many cut cupmarks, reached by rock-cut steps
features.period: not dated
features.quote: התגלה בעבר משטח סלע שחצובים בו ספלולים רבים

features.subtype: pit under the Iron Age rooms
features.period: Early Bronze Age sherds
features.quote: נמצא בור קודם להם ובו חרסים מתקופת הברונזה הקדומה

title: ירושלים: חפירות ליד חומת העיר המערבית (Jerusalem, excavations by the western city wall)
author: M. Broshi (with N. Gershon, an assistant named Eliot (surname not given), S. Gibson, J. Sasson)
location_note: About 280 m along the western wall between the Citadel and the south-west corner; no map reference.
notes: Hasmonean wall under the Turkish wall for about 120 m, an earlier tower; Herodian forewall with two towers; Aelia Capitolina wall segments; Ayyubid inscription of al-Mu'azzam Isa of 1202 and demolition debris. Walls not eligible.

title: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, botanical garden, two burial caves)
author: Y. Gat; A. Kloner and Y. Gat (with D. Melamed)
location_note: Botanical garden on Mount Scopus and its north slope; no map reference.

features.subtype: small cave entered by a shaft: chamber 2.5 x 1.5 m with standing pit, two kokhim, a bone place; no finds
features.period: Second Temple period (heading; by its form and location)
features.quote: נראה ששימשה בימי בית שני

features.site: cave b (north slope of the garden)
features.subtype: square chamber about 3 x 3 m with eight kokhim and a slab-lined standing pit; decorated ossuary; rolling stones thrown into the pit by robbers
features.period: not dated in the report (Byzantine sherds in the fill)
features.quote: ושמונה כוכים

title: ירושלים: העופל (Jerusalem, the Ophel, Ir David road)
author: Y. Gat (with A. Abu Khalil)
location_note: Ir David road (Wadi Tilweh), Ophel; no map reference.
notes: Wall segments marked by Bliss; perhaps fortifications of the western hill in the Second Temple period; First and Second Temple sherds. No feature of the eligible classes.

title: ירושלים: אזור הכנסייה הסקוטית (Jerusalem, area of the Scottish church)
author: G. Barkay (with D. Hamilton and A. Abu Khalil)
location_note: Small hill between the road to Mount Zion and the road up to the Scottish church, near the railway station; no map reference.
notes: Large threshold in situ; opus sectile and gilded glass wall-mosaic tesserae of a Byzantine church; Iron Age sherds (8th-7th centuries BCE) without structures. A built, vaulted underground ashlar room south of the graves (entered through a shaft) is a built structure, not coded.

features.subtype: three plastered burial troughs with head-rests and painted crosses, under the paving west of the threshold
features.period: with the Byzantine church
features.quote: נחשפו שלושה משכבי קבורה

title: ירושלים: בית וגן (Jerusalem, Bayit va-Gan, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner and D. Davis
location_note: Girls' school building site, Bayit va-Gan; no map reference.

features.subtype: entrance room with a bone kokh and an unfinished kokh; inner room with arcosolia on three walls and a small bone pit (cooking pot and Herodian lamp)
features.period: end of the Second Temple period and perhaps a short time after
features.quote: נראה שהמערה שימשה בסוף ימי הבית השני

title: ירושלים: מערת האשכולות (Jerusalem, the Cave of the Grapes, cleaning continued)
author: (Department of Antiquities staff)
location_note: Ramot Eshkol; no map reference.
notes: Same cave as HA28-028 and HA53-023. Ornamented facade; ossuaries smashed during the later use; many animal bones; hard packed fill; plan drawn by Macalister in 1900.

features.subtype: burial cave with carved facade in hard limestone
features.period: hewn in the Second Temple period
features.quote: היא נחצבה בימי הבית השני כמערת קבורה

features.subtype: the same cave used for dwelling, animal bones from food
features.period: later periods (not specified)
features.quote: ושימשה למגורים בתקופות מאוחרות יותר

title: ירושלים: אוגוסטה ויקטוריה (Jerusalem, Augusta Victoria, burial cave)
author: Y. Gat (with D. Melamed and D. Stacey)
location_note: East slope of the hill of the Augusta Victoria hospital (a-Tur); no map reference.
notes: Two sarcophagi and a large ossuary in an antiquities shop were probably robbed from this cave.

features.subtype: spacious multi-room cave in soft limestone: entrance hall, rooms with standing pits and kokhim, lamp niches, a room sealed by a rolling stone with three ossuaries
features.period: used for burial from the mid-1st century BCE to the mid-2nd century CE (Herodian lamps, a Roman lamp)
features.quote: שימשה לקבורה החל מאמצע המאה הא

title: ירושלים: כיכר צה"ל (Jerusalem, Kikar Tzahal, Fast hotel site)
author: D. Davis
location_note: Site of the former Fast hotel; no map reference.
notes: Dump soil with First Temple to medieval sherds; 4th-century CE sherds on the rock; Turkish guard house. No feature of the eligible classes.

title: ירושלים: מזרח תלפיות (Jerusalem, East Talpiyot, burial cave)
author: Y. Gat (with D. Stacey, I. Votkin, D. Melamed)
location_note: East Talpiyot (Armon ha-Natziv) building area; no map reference.

features.subtype: two rooms: one square without kokhim, one rectangular with benches; juglet, lamp, jug
features.period: beginning of the 1st century BCE
features.quote: שאפשר לייחס קבר זה לתחילת המאה
